candidate_notes: These are new Stage G research hypotheses, not reconstructions of the original AI/RL bot and not retunes of the rejected Stage E heuristic family.

decision_rules.EXPLORATORY_NO_CREDIBLE_EDGE: Adaptive methods do not beat no-trade and rotation after severe costs.
decision_rules.EXPLORATORY_PROMISING_REQUIRES_FRESH_VAL: Exploratory remainder looks better but data is previously examined.
decision_rules.RESEARCH_INFRASTRUCTURE_ONLY: Insufficient fidelity or no genuine holdout for a trading claim.

hypotheses.H1_regime: Trend proxies may be more suitable in persistent directional regimes; this is untested.
hypotheses.H2_vote: Requiring agreement among distinct proxies may reduce conflicting trades.
hypotheses.H3_weights: Delayed exponential weights may down-weight recently costly proxies.
hypotheses.H4_no_trade: Abstaining when regime is uncertain or spread/ATR is high may cut cost drag.

label: EXPERIMENTAL_ADAPTIVE_ENSEMBLE_OFFLINE
research_question: Does a market-aware adaptive selection or ensemble approach improve net, risk-adjusted outcomes over simple, prespecified benchmarks after realistic costs, without relying on hindsight or excessive model complexity?
secondary_questions: Which regime features are computable without look-ahead?
Does voting improve decision quality versus a single proxy?
Do delayed-outcome exponential weights outperform equal weights?
Does NO TRADE reduce low-quality exposure?
Are any apparent gains concentrated in one pair or short window?
Are improvements robust to severe costs?
Does extra complexity justify itself versus rotation or no-trade?
stop_conditions: No genuine unseen future period exists; do not claim final holdout validation.
Do not retune after viewing remainder results.
A system with zero trades is not profitable.
Sign flip under severe costs rejects an edge claim.
uncertainty: block-bootstrap of trade P&L is not claimed; overlapping holds are dependent
